speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How long have you been experiencing these nosebleeds and skin spots, and do they happen spontaneously or only after minor bumps? Do you have any family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have any fever, recent infections, or signs of fatigue and pallor? Have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes or an enlarged spleen in the abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you currently running a fever, feeling unusually tired, or have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes or an enlarged spleen? Do you recall any recent viral infections before these bleeding symptoms started? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature: 36.8°C (98.2°F); Blood Pressure: 100/60 mmHg; Heart Rate: 90 bpm; Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min. Skin Examination: Diffuse petechiae noted on forearms, legs, and trunk; no significant ecchymosis or active bleeding. Oral Examination: Mild gum bleeding on gentle probing; no ulcers. ENT Examination: No active epistaxis, dried blood at nares. Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No platelet clumping, normal cell morphology. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient

speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: The normal platelet count with defective platelet surface function on your ELISA test strongly points to Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. Do you recall if any previous family members had similar bleeding issues that were passed down?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and confirmed surface deficiency, I need to verify if this is an inherited condition like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. Does your older sibling or any other family member have a history of easy bruising or bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your sibling and parents deny any bleeding history, this lack of family involvement makes Glanzmann's thrombasthenia less likely. I need to rule out other causes, so REQUEST TEST: Flow_Cytometry_for_CD41_and_CD61_antigens.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Flow Cytometry for CD41 and CD61 antigens: Severe deficiency of both GPIIb (CD41) and GPIIIa (CD61) antigens detected on platelet surfaces, confirming Glanzmann's thrombasthenia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The flow cytometry results confirming a severe deficiency of GPIIb and GPIIIa antigens definitively diagnose Glanzmann's thrombasthenia, even without a known family history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
